steps.name: Prepare ranked gene list from DESeq2 results
steps.question: From the DESeq2 treated-vs-control results table (de_results.csv, 12000 genes x 8 columns), build the full ranked list of tested genes (by the Wald statistic) required as input for preranked GSEA, and document the identifier space and coverage.

grounding.reason: Full ranked list (no threshold) built from the Wald statistic per R-0045/R-0099; identifier-space check per R-0101

steps.description: Load de_results.csv, verify it carries gene symbol, base_mean, log2_fold_change, and a Wald statistic (stat) column plus padj; drop only genes with NA statistic (e.g. DESeq2 outlier-flagged or independent-filtering-excluded rows) and report how many were dropped and why. Confirm gene identifiers are HGNC symbols (matching the Hallmark and Reactome gene set files) with no case/alias mismatches; report the fraction of tested genes that fail to match either gene set collection's identifier space. Produce a two-column ranked list (gene symbol, stat) covering all remaining tested genes, sorted descending by stat — this is the full, unthresholded input GSEA preranked analysis requires (no filtering by padj or log2FC). Note in the output that sample_01's ~4x-below-median library size was a QC flag on the original DESeq2 run (already reflected in that table's size-factor normalization) and is not a reason to exclude any gene here.
acceptance_criteria: Ranked list contains every gene from de_results.csv that has a non-NA stat value, with count of any NA/dropped genes reported
Ranked list is sorted descending by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (stat), matching the rank_metric='stat' choice stated in the plan
Report states the identifier space (HGNC symbols) and the fraction of ranked genes that will fail to map onto the Hallmark and Reactome gene symbol sets

steps.name: Preranked GSEA against MSigDB Hallmark gene sets
steps.question: Which of the 50 MSigDB Hallmark gene sets are significantly enriched (up or down) in the AD lesional vs control ranked gene list?

grounding.reason: fgsea/gseapy preranked GSEA on Hallmark first, per R-0048/R-0107; rank_metric=stat is the stated disputed choice per R-0108; size window 15-500 per R-0047

steps.description: Run gseapy.prerank on the ranked list from T1S1 against the MSigDB human Hallmark gene sets (staged reference: 50 HALLMARK_* sets, HGNC symbols, MSigDB 2026.1 release). Use gene set size window 15-500 genes (post-intersection with tested genes), permutation_num=1000, seed=42 for reproducibility, BH-adjusted FDR q-value for significance (report at FDR<0.25, the standard GSEA convention, and separately flag any set also passing FDR<0.05). Report NES, p-value, FDR q-value, and the leading-edge gene list for every significant set. State explicitly in the output that the ranking metric used is the DESeq2 Wald statistic (a stated, disputed choice among stat / signed -log10(p) / shrunken log2FC).
acceptance_criteria: Enrichment run completes against all 50 Hallmark sets with sets outside the 15-500 gene window after intersection excluded and that exclusion count reported
Output table includes NES, p-value, FDR q-value, and leading-edge genes for each tested Hallmark set
Seed (42), permutation count, ranking metric, and gene set collection version (2026.1) are recorded in the output for reproducibility

steps.name: Preranked GSEA against Reactome pathways (follow-up collection)
steps.question: Which Reactome pathways are enriched in the AD lesional vs control ranked gene list, as a mechanistic follow-up to the Hallmark result?

grounding.reason: Reactome as the second collection after Hallmark per R-0098

steps.description: Run gseapy.prerank with the same ranked list (T1S1), same parameters (15-500 gene window, permutation_num=1000, seed=42, rank_metric=stat) against the Reactome human pathway gene sets from the staged reference GMT (ReactomePathways.gmt, filtered to Homo sapiens using the accompanying ReactomePathways.txt index, current Reactome release). Report NES, p-value, FDR q-value, and leading-edge genes for significant pathways (FDR<0.25). This is the curated second-collection pass that resolves a Hallmark hit to a specific pathway.
acceptance_criteria: ReactomePathways.gmt is filtered to Homo sapiens pathways only (using ReactomePathways.txt), and the number of human pathway sets tested is reported
Output table includes NES, p-value, FDR q-value, and leading-edge genes for each significant Reactome pathway (FDR<0.25)
Reactome release/version is recorded in the output alongside the same seed and rank metric used for the Hallmark run

steps.question: What is the consolidated, decision-ready summary of hallmark (and supporting Reactome) pathway enrichment in AD lesional vs control skin, with appropriate caveats?

grounding.reason: Report must state database/version/rank metric/universe/size window (R-0051), method-dependence caveat (R-0055), leading edge per set (R-0105), reproducibility record (R-0086), and collapse redundant sets (R-0052)

steps.description: Combine the Hallmark (T2S1) and Reactome (T2S2) GSEA outputs into one report. Collapse redundant/overlapping significant gene sets into representative groups with shared leading-edge genes noted (keep the full table as supplement). List leading-edge genes per significant set. State the enrichment method-dependence caveat (a different ranking metric or method could give a different set list) and that this is a single-method result, not the only defensible one. State the size of the DE result table used (12000 genes), how many were ranked, the identifier mapping coverage, and note the sample_01 low-depth caveat as inherited from the upstream DESeq2 run. Include the full reproducibility record: gseapy version, seed (42), permutation count, Hallmark collection version (2026.1), Reactome release, and rank metric (DESeq2 Wald statistic).
acceptance_criteria: Report lists all significant Hallmark sets and significant Reactome pathways with NES, FDR, and leading-edge genes
Report explicitly states the ranking-metric choice, the gene-set collection versions, the seed, and the enrichment method-dependence caveat
Report notes the sample_01 low library size QC caveat inherited from the upstream DE analysis

plan.title: AD lesional vs control: Hallmark GSEA from existing DE
plan.analytical_narrative: The DESeq2 results table (de_results.csv, 12000 genes) for the AD lesional vs control contrast already exists, so this plan starts from it rather than re-running differential expression. Step 1 validates and prepares the DE table (checks columns, gene identifier space, the stat/log2FC/padj fields, and the presence of the low-depth sample_01 caveat as a documented QC note rather than a reason to exclude any gene) and builds the full ranked gene list required for preranked GSEA — the Wald statistic (stat) is used as the ranking metric per the disputed-rule choice, since it is signed and scaled by standard error and avoids the noise of unshrunken log2FC or p-value ties. Step 2 runs fgsea-style preranked GSEA (gseapy.prerank, Python per user constraint) against the MSigDB Hallmark human gene sets staged in the reference store, with the standard 15-500 gene set size window, on the full ranked list (no pre-thresholding, per R-0045/R-0107). Step 3 runs the same preranked GSEA against Reactome pathways as the follow-up curated collection (R-0098), to see whether Hallmark hits resolve to specific mechanisms. Step 4 synthesizes both results into a single report: significant Hallmark and Reactome pathways (BH-adjusted FDR < 0.25 per standard GSEA convention, consistent with the ranking-metric disputed choice stated explicitly), leading-edge genes per significant set, redundancy collapsing across overlapping sets, the enrichment method-dependence caveat, and the full reproducibility record (package versions, seed, gene-set collection versions).
